correctness.rationale: The variational formula proves concavity and orbit averaging. A direct orthogonal leaf-aggregate decomposition yields the two-by-two spectral branch and leaf-difference eigenvalues. The strictly increasing lower branch reduces the core to its exact homogeneous unit-budget optimum. The Schur complement characterizes target-gap feasibility with y>r, and the strictly convex scalar budget function has a unique minimizing split. Explicit scaled base weights and uniform leaf rates meet all inequalities at equality. Symbolic characteristic and budget identities, 72 full-spectrum tests, 18 non-edge-transitive prism cases and 810 nonexhaustive asymmetric stress tests reproduced the predictions.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general SDP describes how to solve arbitrary instances but does not by itself state the exact scalar composition formula. Neither the published symmetry reduction nor the unweighted corona spectrum directly gives the optimal leaf/core budget split for all positive costs and every positive integer leaf count.

originality.rationale: The literature supplies general continuous-time spectral-gap convex optimization, fixed unweighted corona Laplacian eigenvalues, and discrete-time symmetry reduction, but none of the inspected relevant sources states an exact optimization lifting identity parameterized by an arbitrary vertex-transitive core unit-budget gap, arbitrary pendant multiplicity and invariant base-edge cost classes. Claim-level comparisons and genuine source inspections support a best-knowledge original explicit transfer law, with residual specialist-coverage risk.
residual_risks: A specialized earlier theorem using graph corona lifting or an SDP dual parametrization may provide a stronger equivalent formula even if the searched phrasing differs.
The 2022 weighted-corona spectral literature, concerned with different spectral invariants, was not exhaustively examined in all full-text instances.
The proof does not assert unrestricted uniqueness and applies only to the stated cost-symmetry class.

value.rationale: The sharp formula reduces infinitely many enlarged continuous-time network-design problems to one scalar base optimum, preserving arbitrary optimal core profiles, and provides the exact positive leaf/core budget division. It holds across leaf multiplicity and distinct orbit costs, including an explicit non-edge-transitive prism family; these structural design and compositional consequences are useful independent of computing an entirely new SDP for each decorated graph.
